## About this site

This site supports review and exam preparation for **PSYC 383 Psychopharmacology**. It follows the same focused structure as the Biochemistry of the Cell study site:

- [**Study Guides**](study-guides/index.qmd) — one guide for each of the 16 lectures, organized around the concepts emphasized in the lecture presentation.
- [**Practice Questions**](practice/index.qmd) — lecture-level question banks plus nine timed practice exams, with answers and explanations hidden until opened.

## How the materials are built

The **lecture presentation is the authority for scope**. The assigned Meyer chapter provides the detailed psychopharmacological explanation and terminology. Web Boxes are treated as supplementary examples where they reinforce lecture material.

Practice questions are generated to cover the full lecture scope. Lecture banks use an approximately **80% multiple-choice / 20% written-response** mix.

## Course sequence

### Part I

- **Lecture 1:** Principles of Pharmacology
- **Lecture 2:** Structure and Function of the Nervous System
- **Lecture 3:** Chemical Signalling in the Nervous System
- **Lecture 4:** Methods of Research in Psychopharmacology

### Part II

- **Lecture 5:** Catecholamines I — Dopamine
- **Lecture 6:** Catecholamines II — Noradrenaline
- **Lecture 7:** Serotonin
- **Lecture 8:** Acetylcholine
- **Lecture 9:** Glutamate
- **Lecture 10:** GABA

### Part III

- **Lecture 11:** Circadian Rhythms and Chronopharmacology
- **Lecture 12:** Drug Addiction and Brain Reward Systems
- **Lecture 13:** Addiction and Psychostimulants
- **Lecture 14:** Alcohol
- **Lecture 15:** Opioids
- **Lecture 16:** Nicotine and Caffeine

## Practice exams

- **Part I:** three 50-minute exams, each with **30 multiple-choice + 4 short-essay questions** (Lectures 1–4).
- **Part II:** three 50-minute exams, each with **45 multiple-choice questions** (Lectures 5–10).
- **Part III:** three 50-minute exams, each with **30 multiple-choice + 4 short-essay questions** (Lectures 11–16).
